pack.name: Core English
pack.description: Expresiones del inglés general: phrasal verbs, collocations y conectores.

expressions.explanation: Use it when you finally find the answer to a question or the cause of a problem.

examples.english: I'm trying to figure out what happened last night.
examples.spanish: Estoy intentando averiguar qué pasó anoche.

examples.english: We still need to figure out why the service keeps failing.
examples.spanish: Todavía necesitamos averiguar por qué el servicio sigue fallando.

expressions.explanation: To delay something until a later moment, usually something you decided to do.

examples.english: I keep putting off writing the summary.
examples.spanish: Sigo aplazando escribir el resumen.

examples.english: They had to put off the launch until Friday.
examples.spanish: Tuvieron que posponer el lanzamiento hasta el viernes.

expressions.explanation: To unexpectedly meet a person or, more often, an obstacle such as a problem or a difficulty.

examples.english: We ran into a problem with the payment integration.
examples.spanish: Nos encontramos con un problema con la pasarela de pago.

examples.english: I ran into an old colleague at the conference.
examples.spanish: Me topé con un antiguo compañero en la conferencia.

expressions.explanation: To examine something carefully in order to understand it or to find the cause of a problem.

examples.english: Someone should look into why the app crashes on Android.
examples.spanish: Alguien debería investigar por qué la app se bloquea en Android.

examples.english: The committee will look into the complaint before replying.
examples.spanish: El comité examinará la queja antes de responder.

expressions.explanation: To refuse an offer, a request or a job. Compare with turning a device down, which means lowering the volume.

examples.english: She turned down the job offer because of the hours.
examples.spanish: Ella rechazó la oferta de empleo por los horarios.

examples.english: He turned down the invitation without giving a reason.
examples.spanish: Él rechazó la invitación sin dar explicaciones.

expressions.explanation: To mention a topic so that people can discuss it, or to raise a child.

examples.english: I want to bring up a concern about the deadline.
examples.spanish: Quiero plantear una inquietud sobre el plazo.

examples.english: Don't bring up that subject again, please.
examples.spanish: No vuelvas a sacar ese tema, por favor.

expressions.explanation: To arrange the equipment or the structure needed for something to work or to exist.

examples.english: It takes ten minutes to set up the new router.
examples.spanish: Tienen diez minutos para montar el router nuevo.

examples.english: She set up a small business while studying.
examples.spanish: Montó un pequeño negocio mientras estudiaba.

expressions.explanation: To start managing a team, a project or a company, either by agreement or because the previous owner left.

examples.english: After her accident, his brother took over the family shop.
examples.spanish: Tras su accidente, su hermano asumió el negocio familiar.

examples.english: The new manager took over the project in March.
examples.spanish: El nuevo gestor se hizo cargo del proyecto en marzo.

expressions.explanation: To perform a task, a plan or a study from beginning to end.

examples.english: The team carried out a survey among 500 employees.
examples.spanish: El equipo realizó una encuesta entre 500 empleados.

examples.english: We carried out the changes without any downtime.
examples.spanish: Aplicamos los cambios sin ninguna interrupción.

expressions.explanation: To succeed in making an idea understood. In British English, get on with means the same thing.

examples.english: I struggled to get the main idea across.
examples.spanish: Me costó transmitir la idea principal.

examples.english: Use a simple example to get the point across.
examples.spanish: Usa un ejemplo sencillo para hacer entender el punto.

expressions.explanation: To accept a bad or unpleasant situation without complaining much about it.

examples.english: I can't put up with this noise any longer.
examples.spanish: No puedo aguantar este ruido ni un minuto más.

examples.english: She put up with the delays for months.
examples.spanish: Aguantó los retrasos durante meses.

expressions.explanation: To produce an idea, a plan or an answer, usually quickly and after thinking.

examples.english: We need a better idea. Can anyone come up with one?
examples.spanish: Necesitamos una idea mejor. ¿Alguien se le ocurre alguna?

examples.english: He never runs out of ideas for the children's stories.
examples.spanish: A él nunca se le acaban las ideas para los cuentos infantiles.

expressions.explanation: To deal with a problem until it is solved, or to organize things.

examples.english: Let's sort out this mess before Friday.
examples.spanish: Arreglemos este desastre antes del viernes.

examples.english: I'm sorting out my notes from the meeting.
examples.spanish: Estoy ordenando mis notas de la reunión.

expressions.explanation: To cancel an event or stop an activity that has been planned.

examples.english: The organizers called off the event because of the storm.
examples.spanish: Los organizadores cancelaron el evento por la tormenta.

examples.english: Management decided to call off the strike.
examples.spanish: La dirección decidió cancelar la huelga.

expressions.explanation: To be clearly better or more noticeable than everything else around you.

examples.english: Her explanations stand out because they are so clear.
examples.spanish: Sus explicaciones destacan porque son muy claras.

examples.english: That red logo stands out from a distance.
examples.spanish: Ese logo rojo destaca a distancia.

expressions.explanation: For a machine or system: to stop working. For a car: to stop in the middle of the journey.

examples.english: The lift broke down on the fifth floor.
examples.spanish: El ascensor se averió en el quinto piso.

examples.english: Our reporting tool breaks down when the data is huge.
examples.spanish: Nuestra herramienta de informes falla cuando los datos son enormes.

expressions.meaning: dejar, entregar (a una persona o un objeto)
expressions.explanation: To take someone or something to a place and leave them there.

examples.english: I'll drop you off at the station on my way home.
examples.spanish: Te dejo en la estación de camino a casa.

examples.english: Can you drop off the parcel at reception?
examples.spanish: ¿Puedes entregar el paquete en recepción?

expressions.explanation: To respect or admire someone. Do not confuse it with look up, which is to search for a word in a dictionary.

examples.english: I grew up looking up to my older brother.
examples.spanish: Creci admirando a mi hermano mayor.

examples.english: New hires look up to senior engineers for guidance.
examples.spanish: Las nuevas incorporaciones admiran a los ingenieros senior y piden su orientación.

expressions.explanation: A standard collocation. In everyday English, decide is more common than make a decision.

examples.english: It's hard to make a decision without more data.
examples.spanish: Es difícil tomar una decisión sin más datos.

examples.english: She made a decision on the spot.
examples.spanish: Tomó una decisión en el momento.

expressions.explanation: To accept that you are the one who must answer for something, usually a mistake or a task.

examples.english: He took responsibility for the mistake and fixed it.
examples.spanish: Asumió la responsabilidad del error y lo arregló.

examples.english: Taking responsibility early saves a lot of drama.
examples.spanish: Asumir la responsabilidad a tiempo ahorra mucho drama.

expressions.explanation: Research is uncountable, so we say do research, never do a research. The verb carry out is also common.

examples.english: We did some research into how competitors price their plans.
examples.spanish: Investigamos cómo la competencia fija sus precios.

examples.english: She does research on language learning at the university.
examples.spanish: Investiga sobre aprendizaje de lenguas en la universidad.

expressions.explanation: To listen or watch carefully because the information matters.

examples.english: Pay attention to the tense in the first exercise.
examples.spanish: Presta atención al tiempo verbal en el primer ejercicio.

examples.english: Nobody pays attention during long meetings.
examples.spanish: Nadie presta atención en las reuniones largas.

expressions.explanation: To reach a decision or an opinion after examining information.

examples.english: It's too early to draw a conclusion from one test.
examples.spanish: Es demasiado pronto para sacar una conclusión de un solo test.

examples.english: The committee drew conclusions from the audit report.
examples.spanish: El comité sacó conclusiones del informe de auditoría.

expressions.meaning: llevar el seguimiento, llevar la cuenta
expressions.explanation: To keep a record of something so that you always know its current state.

examples.english: I keep track of my study hours in a spreadsheet.
examples.spanish: Llevo la cuenta de mis horas de estudio en una hoja de cálculo.

examples.english: Keep track of the versions you install.
examples.spanish: Lleva el seguimiento de las versiones que instalas.

expressions.explanation: A slightly formal way to add information that is relevant and surprising, similar to actually.
patterns: as a matter of fact + clause

examples.english: As a matter of fact, the fix is already in production.
examples.spanish: De hecho, la corrección ya está en producción.

examples.english: I was going to call you. As a matter of fact, I have news.
examples.spanish: Iba a llamarte. De hecho, tengo noticias.

expressions.meaning: a largo plazo, con el tiempo
expressions.explanation: Used to talk about the effect of something over a long period of time.

examples.english: Writing tests saves time in the long run.
examples.spanish: Escribir tests ahorra tiempo a largo plazo.

examples.english: Learning a little every day pays off in the long run.
examples.spanish: Aprender un poco cada día compensa a largo plazo.

expressions.meaning: en realidad, ahora que lo pienso
expressions.explanation: Used to introduce a change of opinion. With you it becomes on second thoughts.

examples.english: On second thought, let's postpone it to next week.
examples.spanish: Ahora que lo pienso, pospongámoslo a la semana que viene.

examples.english: On second thoughts, I'd rather stay home tonight.
examples.spanish: Al final, preferiría quedarme en casa esta noche.

expressions.explanation: A practical rule that is usually true but not exact. Plurals are rules of thumb, not rules of thumbs.
patterns: a + rule of thumb + is that

examples.english: As a rule of thumb, a reply takes two working days.
examples.spanish: Como regla orientativa, una respuesta tarda dos días laborables.

examples.english: The rule of thumb here is: measure before you change anything.
examples.spanish: La regla empírica aquí es: mide antes de cambiar algo.
